title: Repair a dispatch label at the hook every dispatch passes
action: The model-guard hook already reads the dispatch label (model_guard.rs:732, inside log_dispatch) and does nothing but log it. Give it one repair step, on the PreToolUse path before the payload reaches the runtime. When the dispatch names a cell — the worker prompt carries a line 'Assigned cell id: <id>', and for codex the same text is in `message` — resolve that cell record from .bee/cells/<id>.json (fall back to the archive path the cells store uses), and when the label does not already contain the cell's title, rewrite it to the prepared form: for Agent/Task the `description` field, for spawn_agent the `task_name` field. Announce the repair on the same advisory channel the guard already uses for its other repairs — read how ask-guard-autofix words its announcement and match that shape; the user-visible sentence names what changed and why, never bee mechanics. REPAIR, NEVER REFUSE (ask-guard-autofix D1/D2): a label is not worth losing a dispatch over, and no path added here may return a deny. Every resolution failure — no cell id in the prompt, no cell record, an unreadable or unparseable record, a missing label field — leaves the payload untouched and is silent; the hook is fail-open by construction and this step must not change that. Tests: a bare-id label on a cell dispatch is rewritten to carry the title; an already-correct label is left byte-identical; a dispatch naming no cell is untouched; an unreadable cell record is untouched and does not error; and no input added here ever produces a deny verdict.

truths: A hand-written dispatch that never called prepare still ends up labelled
An already-correct label is byte-identical after the hook
Every resolution failure leaves the payload untouched and silent
No path added by this cell can produce a deny
The full declared test suite is green

trace.outcome: Model-guard now repairs a stale/bare dispatch label to the cell's prepared "<id>: <title>" form whenever a dispatch names a cell, fail-open on every resolution failure
